###Strategy

To $\tealE{\text{set up}}$ the equation for solving, Gabi needs to perform the same operation on both sides of the equation.

To $\purpleD{\text{calculate}}$ the solution, Gabi needs to correctly solve the equation she $\tealE{\text{set up}}$.

If Gabi both $\tealE{\text{set up}}$ and $\purpleD{\text{calculated}}$ the solution correctly, then she correctly solved the equation.

Gabi multiplied both sides of the equation by $10$ to get $j$ by itself.

She correctly $\tealE{\text{set up}}$ the equation.

Gabi then evaluated $80\cdot 10$ to get  $800$.

She correctly $\purpleD{\text{calculated}}$ the solution.

question.content:
Gabi tried to solve an equation.

$\begin{align}
\dfrac j{10}&=80\\\\
\dfrac{j}{10} \cdot 10&=80 \cdot10&\tealE{\text{Setting up}}\\\\
j&=800&\purpleD{\text{Calculating}}
\end{align}$
